newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish government agrees pension deal with unions.
newsitem.headline: Spanish government agrees pension deal with unions.

text.p: The Spanish government on Friday approved a pact with unions to guarantee the buying power of pensions and guarantee future pension payments, a government spokesman said.
"It is a measure aimed at reassuring the whole society," Secretary of State for Communication Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

The deal with Workers' Commissions (CCOO) and the general Workers' Union (UGT) includes a plan to separate the sources of pensions financing by 2000, so that employers will no longer pay for non-contributive pensions and some health services.
It changes the way pensions are calculated, so that they are based on the last 15 years of contributions instead of the last eight.
Employers' organisation CEOE did not sign the agreement, saying that maintaining pensions' buying power would imply higher costs for employers.
